summary: libsignal-node lookalike hijacks @whiskeysockets/baileys and auto-follows attacker-controlled WhatsApp channels using the installer's session
details: @dreamguyxeon/libsignal-node presents itself as a fork of libsignal-node (description 'Modified libsignal for Node.js', README copied from ForstaLabs/libsignal-node), but on require() its index.js schedules install.js, which locates @whiskeysockets/baileys inside node_modules and overwrites lib/Socket/newsletter.js with a bundled MODIFIED_NEWSLETTER_JS payload, dropping a.cache sentinel and calling process.exit(0). The replacement newsletter.js, executed every time baileys loads afterward, fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DGXeon13/strings/refs/heads/main/strings.json (a mutable main branch on a GitHub account unrelated to the baileys or libsignal publishers) and iterates the returned newsletter IDs, invoking newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) against the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session. The result is persistent dependency-tree hijack of an unrelated sibling package combined with a covert, remote-controlled action channel that uses the installer's WhatsApp identity to follow attacker-chosen channels. The advertised libsignal purpose has no relationship to baileys' newsletter code, and the mutation is undocumented and unconditional.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
